key_insight: The paper derives two microscopic superconducting pairing kernels on doped Kitaev honeycomb—one spin-glue odd-parity and one phonon-glue even-parity—and shows that bond-star geometry, not the glue itself, fixes the chirality/parity structure and topological response.
engineering_relevance: It provides a symmetry-based recipe for designing topological superconducting states with predictable Chern number, nodal structure, Kerr rotation, and thermal Hall sign by engineering bond geometry and excitation channel.
method: Derive an odd-parity spin-triplet kernel from the pure Kitaev flux-sector selection rule, with bond-diagonal, separable, rank-one form and anisotropic bond-locked d-vector.
Derive an even-parity d+id singlet kernel from the C3 little-group selection rule of a zone-corner chiral phonon, including an explicit Cooper-channel momentum constraint.
Prove a general odd-fold bond-star theorem showing parity alternation in chiral form factors and mixed singlet-triplet composition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical computation of the bond factor rα≈0.24, analytical use of the Hellmann–Feynman theorem, and explicit topological predictions such as C=±2 or ±4 with sign reversal under pump helicity reversal.
watch_item: The results are symmetry- and model-derived rather than experimentally validated here, so realizability will depend on whether the assumed bond-local kernels and momentum-selection conditions hold in a physical material.
paper_title: Two superconducting pairing models with a Kitaev spin-liquid glue: microscopic kernel and parity alternation on odd-fold bond stars
